title: Europe Records Highest-Ever Q1 BEV Market Share at 19% — March 2026 Its Best Month Yet
detail: Battery electric vehicle (BEV) sales in Europe reached their highest-ever Q1 market share of 19% in early 2026, with March 2026 being the continent's strongest single month for BEV registrations on record, according to ICCT data published April 30. France led Q1 growth with +50% YoY in BEV sales, Germany +41%. Austria, Belgium, Finland, Italy, Portugal, and Spain also posted record BEV months. Individual model highlights included the Skoda Elroq (11,672 units, +146% YoY), Renault Alpine A290 (9,888 units), and Mercedes CLA EV (6,942 units). Globally, Q1 2026 EV sales totaled 4 million units — matching full-year figures from just a few years earlier. The surge was driven by 30+ new BEV models entering the European market in Q1 2026 at more accessible price points (€20,000–30,000), opening the market beyond premium segments. BloombergNEF notes that EV manufacturing scale and LFP battery adoption are now consistently delivering entry-level models below the psychological €25,000 threshold, with mass-market price parity expected in Europe by 2027–2028.

title: Carbon Brief Analysis: Santa Marta Summit Launches Three Fossil Fuel Phase-Out Workstreams, Next Meeting in Tuvalu
detail: Carbon Brief and Climate Change News published detailed analysis on April 30 of the key outcomes from the First International Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels in Santa Marta, Colombia (April 24–29, 2026). The summit established three formal workstreams: (1) a technical workstream to map concrete pathways for reducing fossil fuel demand sector-by-sector; (2) a finance workstream to design transition finance mechanisms for developing-nation fossil fuel workers and communities; and (3) a legal workstream to develop the architecture of a potential future binding treaty instrument. Fifty-seven countries representing roughly one-third of global GDP participated. The follow-up conference was confirmed for Tuvalu in 2027, co-hosted by Tuvalu and Ireland. A new Science Panel for the Global Energy Transition (SPGET) — led by Johan Rockström (Potsdam Institute) and Carlos Nobre (University of São Paulo) — was formally launched and will report to both the Santa Marta process and COP31. Outcomes are designed to feed into updated NDC submissions due under the Paris Agreement's Global Stocktake cycle before COP31 in 2028.
